name: Restorative Justice
region: Global (Indigenous traditions, New Zealand, South Africa, Canada)
summary: Justice frameworks centred on repairing harm through dialogue between victims, offenders, and community rather than punitive retribution.

claims.statement: Restorative justice reduces recidivism compared to conventional criminal justice systems
Indigenous peacemaking circles predate colonial legal systems by centuries and remain in active use
South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission demonstrated restorative principles at national scale

evidence.source: Sherman & Strang (2007) Restorative Justice: The Evidence, Smith Institute
Latimer, Dowden & Muise (2005) The Effectiveness of Restorative Justice Practices, Prison Journal 85(2)
Navajo Peacemaking Courts, documented by Yazzie & Zion (1996)
Maori family group conferencing model adopted in New Zealand Children, Young Persons, and Their Families Act 1989
Truth and Reconciliation Commission of South Africa Report (1998), Volumes 1-5

notes: Rooted in Ubuntu philosophy and Indigenous peacemaking; represents ethics as functional infrastructure rather than abstract principle.
